text: Lastochkyne, a village west of Avdiivka in Pokrovsk raion, has been renamed Krynychne.
notes: Rename dated only as 2016–2024 in the preamble.

text: Sieverne, a village west of Avdiivka in Pokrovsk raion, has been renamed Pivnichne.
The Krasnohorivka north of Avdiivka has been renamed Yasnohorivka; it is not the town of Krasnohorivka west of Donetsk.
Pervomaiske, southwest of Avdiivka, has been renamed Avdiivske.
Avdiivka is a small industrial city of about 32,000 pre-war residents, under 10 km from Donetsk.
Avdiivka was home to the Avdiivka Coke and Chemical Plant (AKHZ, 'Koksokhim'), the largest coke producer in Ukraine.
Avdiivka had been a fortified front-line salient since 2014, with reinforced-concrete positions, trenches and tunnels.
By autumn 2023 Avdiivka was already semi-encircled by Russian forces.
At dawn on 10 October 2023 Russia opened the Avdiivka offensive with what Ukrainian soldiers called its strongest fire preparation in Donbas of the war.

In October 2023 Russian armoured assault groups attacked Avdiivka's northern flank (Krasnohorivka–Stepove–Berdychi, towards the coke plant) and southern flank (Sieverne, Vodiane–Opytne) to encircle the garrison.
A second Russian mechanised wave against Avdiivka followed on 19–20 October 2023.
notes: The block cites OSW and ISW 11 Oct for the pincer sentences; the second-wave sentence carries no separate citation.

text: Satellite counts show Russia lost at least 109 vehicles at Avdiivka in the first ten days of the offensive (10–20 October 2023).
ISW judged that Russia's October 2023 vehicle losses at Avdiivka were larger than those at Vuhledar.
From November 2023 Russia switched to dismounted infantry assaults at Avdiivka.
Russian forces took the waste heap (terrikon) north of Avdiivka in late October 2023.
Russian forces took Avdiivka's fortified southeastern industrial zone ('promka') between mid-November and early December 2023.
The Avdiivka coke plant held through the November 2023 – January 2024 grind.
About 15 January 2024 Russian troops came up a service-water pipe behind the 'Tsarska Okhota' strongpoint in southern Avdiivka.
In early February 2024 Russian troops infiltrated through Avdiivka's northern dachas between the quarry and the lakes, bypassing the coke plant.
On 12–14 February 2024 Russian troops reached Industrialnyi Avenue and cut Avdiivka in two, with the coke plant to the north and the centre to the south.
By 14 February 2024 the main supply road into Avdiivka through Lastochkyne was lost.
The UK MoD reported Russian glide bombs falling on Avdiivka at 30–50 a day by early February 2024.
Ukrainian units reported about 60 Russian glide bombs a day on Avdiivka by mid-February 2024.
Ukrainian guns at Avdiivka were starved of ammunition by the stalled US supplemental.
The 3rd Assault Brigade was rushed into Avdiivka as the last reserve, and the exhausted 110th Mechanised Brigade began to rotate out.
Zenit, the southern bastion of Avdiivka, was abandoned on 14–15 February 2024.
On the night of 16–17 February 2024 the new commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi, announced the withdrawal from Avdiivka 'to avoid encirclement'.
The Ukrainian withdrawal from Avdiivka was completed on 17 February 2024.
Avdiivka held about four months: the battle ran from 10 October 2023 to the Ukrainian withdrawal on 17 February 2024.
The Avdiivka coke plant held to the end; the 25th Assault Battalion of the 47th Mechanised Brigade was the last unit to leave it.
The 3rd Assault Brigade had largely evacuated the Avdiivka coke plant by 05:00 on 17 February 2024.
Ukrainian troops said no one was left behind at the Avdiivka coke plant.
There was no operational encirclement at Avdiivka: ISW and the Ukrainian command say the garrison withdrew 'in mainly good order'.
The Ukrainian withdrawal from Avdiivka was nonetheless late and costly in places, above all at Zenit.
The Russian MoD claimed an 8.6 km advance in depth at Avdiivka.
The Russian MoD's claimed gain at Avdiivka was about 32 km².
Ukrainska Pravda says the Avdiivka front line moved back 7–13 km.
Per the Tavria group, the Russian gain at Avdiivka in the first two months was only 1.5–2 km.
Tarnavskyi claimed Russian losses at Avdiivka of over 47,000 personnel, 364 tanks, 748 AFVs, 248 artillery systems and 5 aircraft.
Ukrainian sources put Russian losses at Avdiivka at 'almost 50,000'.
The Tavria group, via The Insider, claimed 17,000 Russians killed and 30,000 wounded at Avdiivka.
The Russian milblogger Andrei 'Murz' Morozov put Russian irrecoverable losses at Avdiivka at 16,000 and lost equipment at 300 units.
The BBC Russian Service confirmed 6,641 Russian dead at Avdiivka by name, a floor rather than an estimate.
A US estimate put Russian killed and wounded at Avdiivka at 13,000 for October–December 2023 alone.
ISW summarised Ukrainian and Russian estimates of Russian losses at Avdiivka as ranging from 16,000 to 47,000; the Russian cost is contested.
Naalsio visually confirmed 690 Russian vehicles lost at Avdiivka by 23 February 2024: 465 destroyed, 197 abandoned and 28 damaged.
The Insider puts Russian equipment losses at Avdiivka at about nine times Ukraine's.
Tarnavskyi admitted that 'a certain number' of Ukrainian soldiers were captured at the final stage of the Avdiivka withdrawal.
Lykhovii said the number of Ukrainians captured at Avdiivka was not in the 'hundreds' and that the day's losses were 'similar to the average daily losses'.
US officials told the Washington Post that Ukrainian officials privately estimated about 100 Ukrainians captured at Avdiivka (via LWJ).
Mordvichev claimed about 200 Ukrainians surrendered at Avdiivka, with 100 more expected.
The NYT cited two soldiers saying 850–1,000 Ukrainians were captured or unaccounted for at Avdiivka, a figure that includes the killed, wounded and missing.

observations.subject: captured or unaccounted for, incl. killed, wounded and missing

text: Shoigu claimed over 1,500 Ukrainian losses in 24 hours at Avdiivka.
ISW saw no footage supporting mass captures of Ukrainians at Avdiivka.
LWJ judges that 'the bulk of the Ukrainian force ... escaped the pocket' at Avdiivka.

cites.quote: the bulk of the Ukrainian force ... escaped the pocket

text: After Avdiivka fell, Lastochkyne was lost on 24–26 February 2024.
Stepove and Sieverne were lost on 27 February 2024.
Tarnavskyi said the line west of Avdiivka stabilised on Tonenke–Orlivka–Berdychi.
Ukraine claimed 10 Su-34s, 2 Su-35s and an A-50 shot down in February 2024.
The 110th Mechanised Brigade began its defence of Avdiivka in March 2022 and was not rotated for almost two years.
On 9 October 2023 localised Russian attacks started northwest of Avdiivka (Ocheretyne, Tonenke, Berdychi) and southwest (Vodiane–Opytne).
At dawn on 10 October 2023 the main Russian offensive on Avdiivka opened with heavy artillery, thermobaric and incendiary rockets and massed air strikes, aimed above all at the coke plant.
On 10 October 2023 Russian 1st Army Corps assault groups tried to reach the Avdiivka garrison's rear at Berdychi and Stepove.
On 10–11 October 2023 up to three Russian battalions with tanks attacked at Avdiivka.
On 10–11 October 2023 the Ukrainian General Staff named three motor-rifle brigades of the 8th Combined Arms Army in the Avdiivka attack.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Russian advances near Sieverne, Stepove and Krasnohorivka were confirmed on 10–11 October 2023.
Ukraine said it knew in advance of the October 2023 Russian offensive on Avdiivka.
Perpetua's geolocated tally for 10 October 2023 at Avdiivka was 70 Russian and 15 Ukrainian vehicles destroyed.
Ukraine claimed 34 Russian tanks destroyed at Avdiivka in 20 hours on 10 October 2023.
On 11 October 2023 Khodakovsky claimed the Avdiivka slag heap was 'firmly' Russian, then walked the claim back.
ISW assessed on 12 October 2023 that Russian forces had taken 4.52 km² near Avdiivka.
On 12 October 2023 ISW put Russian forces 3.32 km from the O0562 road from the south and 5.25 km from the north.

observations.subject: Russian line to O0562, from the south
Russian line to O0562, from the north

text: By 12 October 2023 Russia had lost at least a BTG's worth of armour at Avdiivka, per ISW.
On 12 October 2023 Ukraine dropped a road bridge between Yasynuvata and Horlivka.
On 13 October 2023 the 129th Territorial Defence Brigade said it still held the Avdiivka slag heap and the coke plant.
ISW saw no evidence of a Russian capture of the Avdiivka coke plant on 13 October 2023.
On 13 October 2023 Russian milbloggers were told to stop detailing the fighting at Avdiivka.
About 16 October 2023 a Russian frontal assault on the Avdiivka terrikon failed under drones and fire from the 110th Mechanised Brigade and the 55th Artillery Brigade.
About 16 October 2023 Barabash counted 15 Russian assaults a day at Avdiivka, down from about 60 in mid-week.
On 17–18 October 2023 Russian troops pushed along Soborna Street towards the fortified 'Tsarska Okhota' restaurant on Avdiivka's southern outskirts.
On 19 October 2023 the Russian 1st Motor Rifle Brigade assaulted Tsarska Okhota, and 'Kluny' gained ground north of Spartak.
On 19 October 2023 Tarnavskyi said 5 Russian aircraft had been downed in 10 days at Avdiivka.
On 19–20 October 2023 the second Russian mechanised wave hit Avdiivka.
The Ukrainian General Staff claimed almost 50 Russian tanks and over 100 AFVs destroyed at Avdiivka in a day on 19–20 October 2023.

claimants.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Ukrainian soldiers claimed 200 Russian AFVs destroyed at Avdiivka in four days around 19–20 October 2023.
Satellite imagery confirms 109 Russian vehicles lost at Avdiivka from 10 to 20 October 2023; ground estimates put it near 200.
On 21–24 October 2023 Russian forces made marginal gains at the Avdiivka waste heap, and the 114th Motor Rifle Brigade reached its northwestern part.
On 22 October 2023 Russia paused to regroup at Avdiivka and funnelled in more units, including mobilised regiments and the 57th Motor Rifle Regiment.
On 26 October 2023 Shtupun claimed 5,000 Russian casualties and 400 armoured vehicles lost near Avdiivka and Marinka since 10 October.
On 26 October 2023 ISW assessed that Russian losses at Avdiivka exceeded those at Vuhledar.
On 28 October 2023 Russia claimed the Avdiivka waste heap; Wikipedia dates its capture to this day.
On 28 October 2023 Butusov put Russian troops 600 m from Avdiivka's northern industrial area.

observations.subject: Russian troops to the northern industrial area

text: On 29 October 2023 Shtupun put 40,000 Russian personnel on the Avdiivka axis.

observations.subject: Russian personnel on the Avdiivka axis

text: On 29 October 2023 Mashovets listed 12 Russian motor-rifle brigades and 16 mobilisation regiments on the Avdiivka axis.
By 30 October 2023 Russian forces were confirmed in Novoselivka Druha, with claims in Avdiivka's 'Khimik' micro-district.
By 30 October 2023 the sixth Russian Su-25 had been downed near Avdiivka since 10 October.
By 30 October 2023 Russian Storm-Z units were being prepared for 'meat assaults' at Avdiivka.
On 3–4 November 2023 Russian forces reached the railway southeast of Stepove.
On 3–4 November 2023 the UK MoD counted about 200 Russian armoured vehicles lost at Avdiivka and saw a switch to dismounted assaults.
On 3–4 November 2023 a 160 m tunnel mine at Avdiivka was claimed.
notes: Claimant not named in the timeline row.

text: On 10 November 2023 Zaluzhnyi claimed Russian losses at Avdiivka in one month of about 10,000 men, 100+ tanks, 250 armoured vehicles and 7 Su-25s.
Footage from about 10 November 2023 showed Russian troops in eastern Stepove.
On 14 November 2023 Russian forces gained their first confirmed foothold in the Avdiivka industrial zone near Yasynuvata Lane.
On 17 November 2023 Russian milbloggers claimed 60% of the Avdiivka industrial zone.

observations.subject: share of the industrial zone claimed

text: On 17 November 2023 the UK MoD saw a Russian pincer at Avdiivka but said the coke plant gave Ukraine a 'localized defensive advantage'.
On 20–21 November 2023 a Russian breakthrough near the Yasynuvata-2 station was claimed, snow started, and a Ukrainian counterattack failed.
On 22 November 2023 a Bradley-supported Ukrainian counterattack retook positions on the Stepove rail line.
On 23–25 November 2023 Tarnavskyi announced a Russian 'third wave' at Avdiivka.
On 25–27 November 2023 Russia claimed the whole Avdiivka industrial zone.
On 25–27 November 2023 Barabash said the Avdiivka coke plant was 'almost completely destroyed'.
On 28 November 2023 armour of the Russian 239th Tank Regiment (90th Tank Division) was committed in the Avdiivka industrial area.
On 1–4 December 2023 Ukraine counterattacked south of Stepove, while Russia gained ground near the reservoir north of Avdiivka.
The Avdiivka industrial zone (promka) was fully Russian-held by 4 December 2023.
About 5 December 2023 the 67th Mechanised Brigade stormed treeline strongpoints near the Avdiivka coke plant behind Bradleys.
On 15 December 2023 Frontelligence counted over 211 Russian vehicles lost at Avdiivka from 10 October to 28 November, half of them in the first three weeks.

observations.subject: share lost in the first three weeks

text: On 20 December 2023 Shtupun said Russia had gained 1.5–2 km in two months for about 25,000 casualties, 80% of them on the Avdiivka axis.

observations.subject: share of casualties on the Avdiivka axis

text: About 27 December 2023 at Stepove a Russian reinforced battalion lost up to 21 tanks and 14 IFVs/APCs in a day.
On 11–12 January 2024 two Bradleys mission-killed a T-90M near Stepove (vignette v02).
About 15 January 2024 Russian assault groups used the empty 1.3–1.4 m service-water pipe to reach the rear of Avdiivka's southern positions.
On 19–20 January 2024 Tarnavskyi reported no Russian airstrikes at Avdiivka for two days after a week of heavy KAB use.
On 20–21 January 2024 Russian forces took the Tsarska Okhota area and pushed up Soborna and Sportyvna streets in Avdiivka; the Skotovata dachas were claimed.
On 23 January 2024 Barabash said Tsarska Okhota was 'breached… but they were driven out'.

cites.quote: breached… but they were driven out

text: On 25 January 2024 Russian video showed men with cutting torches in a tunnel at Avdiivka.
On 25 January 2024 Ukrainian forces counterattacked at Tsarska Okhota.
On 25 January 2024 ISW assessed that Russia was now fighting 'block-by-block' in Avdiivka.
On 27 January 2024 Naalsio counted 574 Russian vehicles lost at Avdiivka against 44 Ukrainian.
On 27 January 2024 the UK MoD called Avdiivka Russia's 'main priority'.
On 1–2 February 2024 Russian forces broke into Avdiivka's northern dachas ('Ivushka') and advanced east of Opytne, deepening the encirclement of Zenit.
On 5 February 2024 the UK MoD said Russian glide-bomb strikes on Avdiivka had risen to 30–50 a day, about 600 in four weeks.
On 5 February 2024 Russian troops were about 1 km from the mouth of the O0542 at Avdiivka.

observations.subject: Russian troops to the mouth of the O0542

text: On 6 February 2024 Russian forces advanced in northern Avdiivka.
On 6 February 2024 Ukrainian SSO soldiers said the Avdiivka pipe was still in Russian use.
On 8 February 2024 Syrskyi replaced Zaluzhnyi as Ukraine's commander-in-chief.
On 8 February 2024 fighting reached Avdiivka's residential north, with the Russian aim of cutting off the coke plant and the main GLOC.
On 8 February 2024 941 residents remained in Avdiivka.
On 10 February 2024 Tarnavskyi said Russia sought control of Avdiivka's northern supply routes and that Ukraine was 'pulling up fresh and effective forces'.

cites.quote: pulling up fresh and effective forces

text: On 10–11 February 2024 thick fog helped the Russian advance at Avdiivka, per DeepState.
The 3rd Assault Brigade arrived at Avdiivka between 3 and 15 February 2024; reported dates are contested: 3 February (Butusov), 4 February (its deputy commander) and 12–13 February (Kyiv Post).
On 15 February 2024 the 3rd Assault Brigade confirmed its 'urgent' redeployment to Avdiivka.
On 12–14 February 2024 Russian forces reached Industrialnyi Avenue and the 'Avtobaza', cutting Avdiivka in half.
On 12–14 February 2024 the main road into Avdiivka through Lastochkyne was lost.
On 13 February 2024 some 110th Mechanised Brigade units were rotated out because the brigade 'no longer has sufficient capabilities to hold the city'.

cites.quote: no longer has sufficient capabilities to hold the city

text: On 13 February 2024 Russian milbloggers claimed up to 60 KABs in a day on Avdiivka.
At about 21:00 on 13 February 2024 the Zenit garrison was told to make its way back towards Avdiivka 'on their own'.
On 14 February 2024 ISW confirmed Russian control of at least 15.4% of Avdiivka.
On 14 February 2024 Tarnavskyi reported a record 73 airstrikes in the Tavria sector.
On the night of 14–15 February 2024 small groups walked about 1 km north from Zenit in the dark under fire, and some were lost.
At 06:00 on 15 February 2024 the last men left the Zenit bunker; six wounded stayed behind, told no evacuation was coming.

observations.subject: wounded left in the Zenit bunker

text: The Russian 1st 'Slavic' Brigade took Zenit by the afternoon of 15 February 2024.
On 15 February 2024 Kirby said Avdiivka 'is at risk' because Ukrainians were 'running out of artillery ammunition'.
On 15 February 2024 ISW saw a Russian 'tactical turning movement' at Avdiivka.
On 15 February 2024 3rd Assault Brigade Bradleys pushed Russian troops 150 m back from the Avdiivka supply road.
On 16 February 2024 Tarnavskyi announced the move away from Zenit.
On 16 February 2024 the 3rd Assault Brigade reported about 15,000 Russians in its Avdiivka sector and 60 bombs a day.

observations.subject: Russian troops in the 3rd Assault's sector

text: On 16 February 2024 Russian forces took Avdiivka's city park and the Donetsk Filtration Station.
At about 01:00 on 17 February 2024 Syrskyi announced the withdrawal from Avdiivka to 'more favourable lines' to avoid encirclement, before it was complete.
By 05:00 on 17 February 2024 the 3rd Assault Brigade had largely left the Avdiivka coke plant, and the 47th's 25th Assault Battalion was the last out.
The 53rd Mechanised Brigade left Avdiivka's 9th quarter after dawn on 17 February 2024.
On 17 February 2024 60 KABs fell in a day at Avdiivka.
notes: Section 5 attributes the 17 Feb figure to 'a brigade'.

text: On 17 February 2024 Russian flags went up at the Avdiivka coke plant and the city administration.
On 17 February 2024 Ukraine claimed two Su-34s and a Su-35 shot down over Donetsk Oblast.
Lykhovii said that by the evening of 17 February 2024 all threatened units were out of Avdiivka.
On 18 February 2024 Tarnavskyi claimed 47,000+ Russian losses at Avdiivka, and the Russian MoD claimed an 8.6 km advance.
On 18 February 2024 video appeared of six wounded Ukrainian POWs executed near Avdiivka.
On 18 February 2024 Ukraine claimed a Su-34 shot down in the Luhansk direction.
At about 09:16 on 19 February 2024 Ukraine claimed a Su-34 and a Su-35S near the Azov coast.
On 20 February 2024 the NYT reported 850–1,000 Ukrainians captured or unaccounted for at Avdiivka.
On 20 February 2024 the 110th Mechanised Brigade said its Zenit wounded were shot despite a Russian promise to evacuate them.
On 21 February 2024 Lykhovii denied that 'hundreds' of Ukrainians had been captured at Avdiivka.
Andrei 'Murz' Morozov died on 21 February 2024 after being ordered to delete his post claiming 16,000 Russian dead at Avdiivka.
On 21 February 2024 Ihnat said seven Su-34s and Su-35s had been downed since 16 February.
On 23 February 2024 a second Russian A-50 was downed.
On 23 February 2024 Russian milbloggers blamed friendly fire for the A-50 and Su-34 losses.
Lastochkyne was lost between 24 February 2024 (Wikipedia) and 26 February 2024 (Kyiv Independent).
Around 24–26 February 2024 Mordvichev claimed 200 Ukrainians had surrendered at Avdiivka.
On 27 February 2024 Ukraine withdrew from Stepove and Sieverne.
The 110th Mechanised Brigade was fully rotated out by 27 February 2024.
On 27 February 2024 two more Russian Su-34s were downed.
On 1 March 2024 the Ukrainian MoD tallied 13 Russian aircraft downed in February 2024: 10 Su-34s, 2 Su-35s and 1 A-50.

A box of about 20 × 15 km holds the Avdiivka diorama: from Berdychi and Krasnohorivka in the north to Opytne and Vodiane in the south, and from Tonenke and Orlivka in the west to Kamianka and the industrial zone in the east.
notes: The box sentence carries no citation of its own; it is the file's framing of the salient.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

text: The Avdiivka industrial zone, on a hill, had been the first line since 2014.
Zenit, a former air-defence base, is not in OSM; it lies '1–2 km south of the city' of Avdiivka.
Zenit had concrete structures and a two-storey bunker; 'if Zenit falls, Avdiivka falls'.
Stepove is at 48.1959, 37.6790 (OSM), at about 204 m (SRTM), 8.5 km NW of the Avdiivka town node and 3.3 km NNW of the coke plant.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

text: Stepove was Avdiivka's northern flank and the Bradley kill zone.
Krasnohorivka (Yasnohorivka) is at 48.2067, 37.7245 (OSM), at about 193 m (SRTM), 8.3 km NNW of the Avdiivka town node.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

text: Krasnohorivka (Yasnohorivka) was the start line of the Russian northern pincer and was captured on 3 November 2023 per DeepState.
Vesele is at 48.1876, 37.7550 (OSM), 6.0 km north of the Avdiivka town node.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

text: Kamianka is at 48.1735, 37.7857 (OSM), 5.3 km north-northeast of the Avdiivka town node.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

notes: geo: 37.7857,48.1735; the table gives 6.0 / 5.3 km N–NNE for Vesele / Kamianka

text: Vesele and Kamianka were the Russian start lines north and northeast of Avdiivka.
The centre of Donetsk is at 47.98, 37.76, about 17 km south of Avdiivka.

observations.subject: great-circle distance from the Avdiivka town node

text: Donetsk was the Russian logistics hub that the Avdiivka salient overlooked.
The Avdiivka salient is flat and open apart from the coal and coke spoil heaps.
The open field between Stepove and the railway was a kill zone.
Treelines and concrete walls along the rails north of the Avdiivka coke plant gave Ukraine fire control.
Euromaidan Press calls the Avdiivka terrikon a 'forty-meter-high slag heap'.
Kyiv Post's 'some 150 meters tall' for the Avdiivka terrikon is not supported by SRTM, which shows a top of about 231 m against about 180–200 m around the base, so about 30–50 m of relief.

observations.note: Kyiv Post figure, not supported by SRTM

text: The Avdiivka terrikon's defenders 'saw every Russian move from the heights', and its steep face stopped assaults.

cites.quote: saw every Russian move from the heights

text: The Avdiivka coke plant's tunnels, railways and alleys made it 'near-perfect' defensive ground.
Hundreds of Ukrainian troops fell back into the Avdiivka coke plant in January 2024.

observations.subject: Ukrainian troops falling back into the plant

text: The Avdiivka coke plant reportedly held about 1,000 Ukrainian troops in the last days.
Barabash said bombing had left the Avdiivka coke plant 'almost completely destroyed', so it was 'not as easy to hold ... as when it was like a fortress'.

cites.quote: not as easy to hold ... as when it was like a fortress

text: Russian sources say the Avdiivka industrial zone sits on a slight hill, from which artillery could be adjusted onto the city.
SRTM gives about 248 m at the Avdiivka industrial zone against about 219 m at the town node.
The Avdiivka pipe is the main service-water pipe that fed the Donetsk filtration station, about 1.3–1.4 m high, and was mostly empty because the city's water had been cut since late 2021.
Russian sources describe the Avdiivka pipe as a flooded 0.5 m drainage pipe and a 2 km infiltration.
United24 gives the Avdiivka pipe as 3.7 km long and up to 1.4 m high.
Lakes and the flooded quarry lie north and northeast of the Avdiivka centre.
After Avdiivka fell, the water west of the city between Berdychi, Semenivka and Orlivka was expected to slow the Russian advance.
The O0542 (H0542) was the main supply route and the only paved road into Avdiivka, running from the west through Lastochkyne, past the famous city sign, into Industrialnyi Avenue.
The Avdiivka–Sieverne road, running past the 9th quarter, was the secondary supply route.
Dirt tracks to Lastochkyne and Sieverne were the last routes into Avdiivka in February 2024.
On 12 October 2023 the O0562 GLOC was 3.3 km from the southern Russian line.

observations.subject: O0562 to the southern Russian line

text: The N20, the Donetsk–Kostiantynivka highway, was partly Russian-held from the start of the battle.
The Avdiivka–Pokrovsk railway runs past Stepove and the coke plant.
Weather for the Avdiivka diorama is ERA5 reanalysis for 48.14 N 37.74 E in Kyiv local time; it is reanalysis, not observations.
On 10–12 October 2023 Avdiivka was dry and mostly clear (cloud 13–55%), with lows about 0 °C and highs of 7–12 °C; sunrise was about 06:40 and sunset about 17:50.
On 19–20 October 2023 Avdiivka was dry, warming to 18 °C, overcast by 20 October, with wind gusting to 33 km/h.
Rain fell at Avdiivka on 26 and 28 October 2023, and milbloggers blamed rain for the lull on 26 October.
In November 2023 mud made many roads around Avdiivka impassable and fog cut aerial reconnaissance.
Morning fog at Avdiivka in autumn 2023 gave windows for Russian infiltration.
On 19–27 November 2023 Avdiivka had its first snow (about 2 cm on 19 November), a frost to −7 °C on 23 November, then 25 mm of rain on 25–26 November and gusts to 38 km/h on 27 November.
Barabash spoke of 'blowing snow and high winds' at Avdiivka in late November 2023.
In January 2024 Avdiivka was mostly around or below freezing and overcast, with light snow (sampled 11, 15 and 20 January).
Kirby expected the frozen ground of late January and February 2024 to favour mechanised attack.
On 5–13 February 2024 Avdiivka had snow on 5 February (about 4 cm), then a thaw: 15 mm of rain on 10 February and highs of 9–14 °C by 11–14 February, under 100% cloud.
Fog covered Avdiivka on 10–11 February 2024.
Barabash said the ground at Avdiivka was too soft for tanks in February 2024.
On 15–17 February 2024, during the withdrawal, a dry hard frost returned to Avdiivka: lows of −2 to −6 °C, highs of 2–3 °C, mostly overcast; sunrise was about 07:35 and sunset about 17:50.
The walk-out from Zenit in February 2024 was 'pitch black'.
A Zenit veteran says it was 'foggy' at the time the evacuation should have happened.
The Avdiivka diorama is a horseshoe salient about 12–15 km wide, projecting about 10 km into Russian lines.

observations.subject: depth the salient projects into Russian lines

text: In November 2023 Kyiv Post described the central Avdiivka pocket as 'funnel-shaped ... less than 15 kilometers wide'.
The Russian Central Grouping of Forces under Col. Gen. Andrei Mordvichev commanded at Avdiivka, and Putin congratulated Mordvichev.
Lt. Gen. Sergei Milchakov reportedly led the DNR 1st Army Corps at Avdiivka; milbloggers complained he went unrecognised.
Formal responsibility for the Avdiivka axis passed to the Russian Central Grouping of Forces after the fall of the city.
Putin on 17 February 2024 credited Russian formations for Avdiivka, including the DNR 1st Army Corps (8th CAA, Southern Military District).
The DNR 1st Army Corps at Avdiivka comprised the 1st ('Slavic'), 9th, 110th, 114th and 132nd Motor Rifle Brigades, the 1454th and 1487th Regiments and the 10th Tank Regiment.
Irregular units were attached to the DNR 1st Army Corps at Avdiivka: 'Kluny', Pyatnashka, Dikaya Diviziya and Arbat (including ex-Wagner men).
Per Kyiv Post, the Russian 114th Motor Rifle Brigade lost 190 dead and 160 wounded at Avdiivka in October 2023 from 1,800–2,000 men.
The Russian 1487th Regiment was reduced to under 30% strength at Avdiivka.
The Russian 41st Combined Arms Army (Central Military District) at Avdiivka fielded the 35th, 55th and 74th Motor Rifle Brigades and the 90th Tank Division (6th, 80th and 239th Tank Regiments).
Ukraine claimed the Russian 90th Tank Division lost 2,500–3,000 men and 250 armoured vehicles at Avdiivka by 12 November 2023.
The Russian 2nd Combined Arms Army (Central Military District) sent the 15th, 21st and 30th Motor Rifle Brigades to Avdiivka, moved laterally from the Lyman direction.
The Russian Volunteer Corps' 60th 'Veterany' Reconnaissance-Assault Brigade led the pipe infiltration at Avdiivka.
HUR says the Russian Volunteer Corps of about 18,000 includes ex-Wagner men and uses Wagner-style assaults.
Russian Storm-Z units at Avdiivka lost 40–70%.
Russian Storm-V units fought at Avdiivka.
Russian GRU spetsnaz and SSO ran night assaults and directed strikes at Avdiivka.
The Russian 24th Spetsnaz Brigade reached the Avdiivka city administration.
At Avdiivka, Russian Su-25s attacked close in, while Su-34s and Su-35s dropped glide bombs from stand-off range.
Shtupun estimated the Russian force at Avdiivka at about 40,000 on 29 October 2023, and again in January 2024.
Lykhovii estimated the Russian force at Avdiivka at about 50,000 in February 2024.
About 15,000 Russian assault troops faced the 3rd Assault Brigade's sector at Avdiivka.

observations.subject: Russian assault troops in the 3rd Assault's sector

text: Foka of the 3rd Assault Brigade said four Russian brigades rotated at Avdiivka in the final weeks with two in reserve, at odds of 1:12 in infantry and 1:10 in artillery and ammunition.
3rd Assault Brigade statements put the odds at Avdiivka at 7:1.
Forbes put two Russian field armies of about 40,000 against about 10,000 Ukrainian defenders at Avdiivka.
The Russian vehicle fleet at Avdiivka was mostly Soviet-era: only about 22% of tank losses were modern T-72B3, T-80BVM or T-90 types, 65 T-80BVs were lost, and 77 of 173 lost IFVs were BMP-1s.
In October 2023 Russia attacked Avdiivka in regiment-plus mechanised waves.
From November 2023 to January 2024 Russian infantry assaulted Avdiivka in groups of 5–7 men at night, then in attacks at sunrise.
In January 2024 the Russian effort at Avdiivka shifted to the pipe and the southern residential block.
In February 2024 Russian armour returned inside Avdiivka, supporting the infantry.
Ukraine's commander-in-chief during the Battle of Avdiivka was Gen. Valerii Zaluzhnyi until 8 February 2024, then Col. Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi.
Brig. Gen. Oleksandr Tarnavskyi commanded the Tavria operational-strategic group at Avdiivka; its spokesmen were Col. Oleksandr Shtupun and, from February 2024, Dmytro Lykhovii.
Maj. Gen. Eduard Moskaliov commanded the Donetsk operational-tactical group at Avdiivka.
Vitalii Barabash was head of the Avdiivka city military administration.
The 110th Mechanised Brigade was the backbone of the Avdiivka defence from March 2022, without rotation.
The 110th Mechanised Brigade held the Avdiivka terrikon in October 2023.
notes: Kyiv Post credits the 129th TD Brigade instead (open questions).

text: The 110th Mechanised Brigade held Zenit to the end.
By February 2024 'grandfathers', elderly vehicle engineers, filled the 110th Mechanised Brigade's line at Avdiivka.
One 110th Mechanised Brigade company at Zenit had no commander, sergeant major or platoon leaders.
Part of the 110th Mechanised Brigade left Avdiivka on 13 February 2024 and the rest on 27 February.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade 'Magura' fielded M2A2 ODS Bradleys and Leopard 2A6s at Avdiivka.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade moved from Zaporizhzhia in October 2023 with little time to recover, and anchored Avdiivka's northern flank around Stepove.
Dmytro Riumshyn commanded the 47th Mechanised Brigade at Avdiivka.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade's 25th Assault Battalion was last out of the Avdiivka coke plant.
The 3rd Separate Assault Brigade was Ukraine's last reserve at Avdiivka, sent 'urgently' while replenishing after Bakhmut; many of its men had not seen combat before.
The 3rd Separate Assault Brigade was led by the former Azov commander.
The 3rd Assault Brigade's 1st Assault Battalion took the Avdiivka residential area facing the quarry; the brigade's deputy commander was Rodion Kudriashov.
The 3rd Assault Brigade's 2nd Assault Battalion was briefly in operational encirclement in the Avdiivka dachas.
The 3rd Assault Brigade used Bradleys on the Avdiivka supply road.
The 2nd Battalion ('Samurai') of the Separate Presidential Brigade held Avdiivka's northern flank and the coke plant for a year.
notes: 'For a year' to the fall; start month implied, not stated.

text: The 53rd Mechanised Brigade was at Sieverne in October 2023.
The 53rd Mechanised Brigade covered the Zenit withdrawal and held Avdiivka's 9th quarter to the last.
The 67th Mechanised Brigade fought with Bradleys at the Avdiivka coke plant.
The 129th Territorial Defence Brigade was at the Avdiivka terrikon and coke plant in October 2023.
The 109th Territorial Defence Brigade fought near Stepove.
The 59th Motorised Brigade's drones fought at Avdiivka.
The 55th Artillery Brigade fought at Avdiivka.
The 25th Airborne Brigade fought at Avdiivka.
SBU 'Alpha' flew FPVs from the Avdiivka coke plant.
HUR, SSO, the Border Guard 'Dozor' unit and the 225th Separate Assault Battalion worked on the Avdiivka evacuation corridor.
Forbes put the Ukrainian defenders of Avdiivka at about 10,000.
On 16 February 2024 Kyiv Post put the Ukrainian men at risk in northern Avdiivka at 'potentially 2,000-4,000 men' of three brigades.

observations.subject: men at risk in the north, of three brigades

text: Russia claimed up to 5,000 Ukrainians were trapped at Avdiivka.
The usual pre-2022 garrison at Zenit was 200–300.
Ukraine's visually confirmed vehicle losses at Avdiivka were 44 by 27 January 2024.
In October 2023 Russian mechanised waves at Avdiivka were columns of 20–40 armoured vehicles led by tanks, 100–200 vehicles in all, driving across open ground into minefields.
Drone spotting, mines, FPVs, ATGMs and artillery stopped the Russian mechanised waves at Avdiivka in October 2023.
Russian counter-battery fire and coordination between units at Avdiivka were poor in October 2023.
After the failed mechanised waves Russia shifted to dismounted assaults at Avdiivka.
Ukraine's defence in depth at Avdiivka rested on concrete positions linked by tunnels.
At Avdiivka Ukrainian gunners used cluster munitions to drive Russian infantry into cover, then artillery to flush them out.
At Avdiivka the 25 mm guns of Ukrainian Bradleys raked treelines and dismounting infantry.
Under the shell economy at Avdiivka, Ukrainian artillery was saved for armour and guns, and FPVs were used against infantry.
ISW calls Avdiivka the first time Russia used glide bombs (KAB, FAB with UMPK) at scale to support advancing infantry, under 'limited and localized air superiority'.
The UK MoD put Russian glide-bomb use at Avdiivka at 30–50 a day by 5 February 2024.
The 3rd Assault Brigade on 16 February 2024 and a Ukrainian brigade on 17 February reported 60 glide bombs a day at Avdiivka.
Foka put Russian glide-bomb use at Avdiivka at 80–110 a day.
Up to 500 glide bombs fell on Avdiivka 'in recent days' before 17 February 2024.
notes: Claimant not named in the text.

text: ISW later withdrew the term 'close air support' for the Avdiivka glide-bomb campaign, since no close coordination with ground units was observed.
Most Ukrainian troops in Avdiivka suffered concussions from the bombing.
At Avdiivka new Ukrainian field positions could not be built under bombing without air defence.
After the second A-50 kill, Russian glide-bomb carriers 'no longer dare[d] to fly too close'.

cites.quote: no longer dare[d] to fly too close

text: On 15 February 2024 a 110th Mechanised Brigade gunner said: 'we have two shells, but ... no charges ... we have run out of shells'.

cites.quote: we have two shells, but ... no charges ... we have run out of shells

text: Ukrainian troops at Avdiivka reported a 5:1 Russian shell advantage in February 2024 and 8–9:1 at worst in late November 2023.
The artillery shell ratio at Avdiivka reached 1:10 in February 2024.
The US supplemental was stalled from October 2023; the Senate passed the $95bn package the week of 15 February 2024, but the House only acted in April.
notes: 'That week' read as the week of the 15 Feb gunner quote.

text: Russian infiltration and tunnelling at Avdiivka evolved from a 160 m mine tunnel under a position in November 2023 to the January 2024 pipe infiltration.
In the Avdiivka pipe infiltration Russian troops used oxygen cylinders for cutting torches, cut exit holes every 100 m, and covered the noise with mortars.

observations.subject: exit holes cut in the pipe

text: Ukraine spotted the Russian gathering at the Avdiivka pipe entry and shelled it, containing the first breach.

mentions.name: detection and artillery strike on the gathering at the pipe entry

text: The same Avdiivka pipe was reused to reach Vinogradniki-2 on 15 February 2024.
Fog on 10–11 February 2024 and in November 2023 grounded Ukrainian drones at Avdiivka, enabling Russian infiltration.
By February 2024 Russian armour at Avdiivka was fitted with EW against drones.
In the last days at Avdiivka Russian jamming cut Ukrainian links to higher echelons.
Before the February 2024 shoot-down spree, the Russian aircraft lost at Avdiivka were attack aircraft forced in close: five in 10 days and seven Su-25s in a month.
Ukrainian troops in Avdiivka asked: 'Make it so that the enemy's aircraft does not fly'.

cites.quote: Make it so that the enemy's aircraft does not fly

text: In the Avdiivka withdrawal Ukrainian units moved in small groups, often on foot along dirt roads, with drones guiding them and artillery covering.
The Tavria group fired almost 400 fire missions to cover the Avdiivka withdrawal.
MWI calls the Avdiivka withdrawal a 'textbook example' of a security force covering the main body.

counter: drone spotting, mines, FPVs, ATGMs and artillery
effect: stopped the October 2023 columns with heavy vehicle losses
rationale: The dossier says drone spotting, mines, FPVs, ATGMs and artillery stopped the October waves, after which Russia shifted to dismounted assaults.

text: In the first wave at Avdiivka (10–12 October 2023), a dawn fire preparation was followed by columns of 20–40 vehicles rolling across flat fields at the salient's shoulders.
A 53rd Mechanised Brigade video from October 2023 shows one Russian column losing two vehicles and 100 men in ten minutes at Avdiivka.
A Russian AFV was filmed falling into water at Avdiivka in October 2023.
Russia lost 70 vehicles in one day in the first wave at Avdiivka.

About 16 October 2023 Russian tanks lined up at the foot of the 40 m wall of the Avdiivka terrikon while infantry tried to climb it under machine guns and drone drops; one soldier got three quarters of the way to the first terrace.
By late October 2023 the Avdiivka terrikon was Russian, but Ukrainian fire stopped Russian troops massing on it.
The Avdiivka coke plant was the anchor of the defence, bombed to ruins but never taken.
A 'Samurai' battalion soldier said: 'The Russians were just banging their heads against the plant'.

cites.quote: The Russians were just banging their heads against the plant

text: A Presidential Brigade soldier said the Russians 'kept throwing themselves at the coke plant, leaving piles of their corpses there'.

cites.quote: kept throwing themselves at the coke plant, leaving piles of their corpses there

text: In November 2023 the Avdiivka industrial zone, a fortified hill of factories held since 2014, was ground away building by building near Yasynuvata-2.
In November 2023 Russian armour moved 'freely' in the northern part of the Avdiivka industrial zone.
In mid-January 2024 Russian men with oxygen cylinders and torches cut exits every 100 m in the Avdiivka pipe under a mortar barrage, then emerged behind Tsarska Okhota.
Ukrainian counterattacks retook some ground after the Russian pipe breach at Avdiivka in January 2024.
At Stepove a T-90M was blinded by Bradley 25 mm fire (vignette v02).
One Bradley killed three MT-LBs in about 30 seconds in the Avdiivka fighting.

On 12–15 February 2024 Russian forces cut the Avdiivka neck by infiltrating through the dachas in fog, jumping the railway, then reaching Industrialnyi Avenue and the 'Brevno' restaurant at the O0542 junction.
The 3rd Assault Brigade's counterattack at Avdiivka pushed back to the railway but could not hold under artillery.
A 3rd Assault Brigade soldier said: 'F**k Avdiivka, we'd rather fight in Mariupol again'.

cites.quote: F**k Avdiivka, we'd rather fight in Mariupol again

text: The order to leave Zenit came at 21:00 on 13 February 2024; men walked 1–2.5 km by night through a 120 m gap, following the sound of a drone.

observations.subject: gap the Zenit garrison walked out through

text: Six wounded Ukrainians and a Russian POW stayed in the Zenit bunker, and the evacuation vehicle never came.

observations.subject: Russian POW left in the bunker

text: A video later showed the execution of the wounded left at Zenit.
On the last night at Avdiivka (16–17 February 2024) Syrskyi announced the withdrawal at about 01:00, and the coke plant was emptied by 05:00 with maps and documents destroyed.
On the last night at Avdiivka the 9th quarter was held until dawn, and a Ukrainian convoy was hit on the 'road of death'.
Ukraine claimed two Su-34s and a Su-35 on 17 February 2024, then more Su-34s on 18, 19, 27 and 29 February, and an A-50 on 23 February.
Cospas-Sarsat beacons from downed Russian aircraft were detected in the Sea of Azov in February 2024.
General Staff spokesman Kovaliov said Ukraine knew about the October 2023 Russian assault on Avdiivka in advance and was ready.

mentions.name: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine

text: Kyiv moved the 47th Mechanised Brigade from Zaporizhzhia to Avdiivka's northern flank in October 2023, though it had little time to recover from the counteroffensive.
The sources link the 47th Mechanised Brigade's Bradleys to repeated defensive successes at Stepove.
After the October 2023 losses at Avdiivka Russia replaced mechanised waves with infantry assaults.

From January 2024 Russia stopped attacking the Avdiivka coke plant and switched to the south and the residential north; Samurai said: 'Perhaps that's why they changed the direction of their main attack'.

cites.quote: Perhaps that's why they changed the direction of their main attack

text: ISW reads Russia's January 2024 switch at Avdiivka as abandoning encirclement for a 'tactical turning movement' through the town.
On 6 February 2024 Ukrainian SSO soldiers said of the Avdiivka pipe: 'The Russians are still using it ... Why our forces don't monitor it, I don't know'.

cites.quote: The Russians are still using it ... Why our forces don't monitor it, I don't know

text: Ukrainska Pravda asked the Tavria group whether control of the Avdiivka pipe had been part of defence planning and received no answer.
The 3rd Assault Brigade was ordered into Avdiivka by Zaluzhnyi, so before 8 February 2024.
Syrskyi was reported moving reserves to Avdiivka on 9 February 2024.
Foka, Butusov and an LWJ source say the 3rd Assault Brigade was committed to Avdiivka to retake and hold.
A 3rd Assault Brigade officer and MWI say the brigade was committed to Avdiivka as the security force for the 110th Mechanised Brigade's withdrawal.
The volunteer commander Yevhen Dykyi gave the 3rd Assault Brigade 'two or three days' to clear the Avdiivka highway, or else it would be 'organizing a corridor'.
The 3rd Assault Brigade's counterattack reached the railway but could not hold.
The order to leave Zenit came on 13 February 2024, telling the garrison to withdraw 'on their own'.
The 110th Mechanised Brigade says it could not reach its wounded at Zenit and asked the POW coordination centre to have Russia evacuate them; Russia agreed, and the men were then shot.

mentions.name: Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War

text: Zenit survivors say: 'instead of getting us out, they sent reinforcements'.

cites.quote: instead of getting us out, they sent reinforcements

text: Two Zenit soldiers say no more than 40% of their company got out.

observations.subject: share of the company that got out

text: The 110th Mechanised Brigade says losses in the Zenit withdrawal were 'minimal'.
On the night of 16–17 February 2024 Syrskyi, nine days in post, ordered the Avdiivka withdrawal and announced it before it was complete, which was unusual compared with Sievierodonetsk and Bakhmut.
Most of Ukrainska Pravda's sources said the Avdiivka withdrawal should have come a day or two earlier.
Four 110th Mechanised Brigade soldiers and Western experts called the Avdiivka withdrawal 'late and disorganized'.
LWJ says the Avdiivka withdrawal 'took too long to commence'.
The Samurai battalion and the 47th's 25th Assault Battalion say they left Avdiivka without losses.
ISW saw a 'relatively controlled withdrawal' from Avdiivka.
MWI says Syrskyi's intent to preserve combat power in the Avdiivka withdrawal was met.
LWJ says Ukraine failed to build a solid line behind Avdiivka, which forced digging under fire.
ISW on 18 February 2024 said imagery 'does not support claims' that there were no prepared positions behind Avdiivka.
Euromaidan Press framed the Avdiivka hold-or-husband debate against Bakhmut, where Syrskyi was criticised for defending strategically unimportant towns.
Lykhovii said Avdiivka 'has fulfilled its mission of draining the Russian reserve'.

cites.quote: has fulfilled its mission of draining the Russian reserve

text: Kirby tied the risk of Avdiivka falling directly to Congress's failure to pass the supplemental.
ISW judged that US aid delays helped Russia on several axes.
DNR nationalists long argued that taking Avdiivka would push Ukrainian guns out of range of Donetsk.
Bielieskov and the Washington Post noted Avdiivka's value as a springboard towards Pokrovsk.
ISW saw the timing of the fall of Avdiivka as a pre-election victory for Putin, and called the fall 'not ... operationally significant'.
In mid-October 2023 Russian milbloggers were told to stop detailing the fighting at Avdiivka.
Russian milbloggers largely ignored the October 2023 vehicle losses at Avdiivka, unlike the outcry after Vuhledar.
Russian soldiers at Avdiivka complained of poor counter-battery fire, foul trenches and a lack of surgeons and body bags in Donetsk.
Shoigu reported 'full control' of Avdiivka on 17 February 2024.
The Russian MoD claimed an 8.6 km advance at Avdiivka.
Shoigu called the capture of Avdiivka a success 'with minimal losses'.
Gerasimov said the capture of Avdiivka took 'a fairly short time' after 'a long period of preparation'.
Putin credited the Russian units listed in the forces section for the capture of Avdiivka.
Shoigu claimed 1,500 Ukrainian losses in 24 hours at Avdiivka, and milbloggers described a chaotic Ukrainian flight.
ISW saw only a handful of POW videos from Avdiivka and called the lack of footage 'very unusual'.
ISW calls the Russian MoD's later campaign about a 'chaotic' Ukrainian withdrawal from Avdiivka an information operation.
Mordvichev claimed 200 Ukrainians surrendered at Avdiivka.
'Murz' (4th Brigade, 2nd LNR Corps) reported 16,000 Russian irrecoverable losses at Avdiivka; he was ordered to delete it and died by suicide on 21 February 2024.
Before his death 'Murz' noted the Russian tank units 'distinguished' themselves by advancing a few kilometres in four months at Avdiivka.
Russian milbloggers complained the MoD ignored Milchakov and the 'Veterany' brigade after Avdiivka.
Russian milbloggers blamed friendly air defence for the Su-34 and A-50 losses in February 2024.
Russian channels claimed 150 special-operations troops used a 0.5 m pipe for 2 km at Avdiivka.
The 'Voenniy Osvedomitel' channel showed video from the Avdiivka tunnel on 25 January 2024.
